gates.evidence: The AOL mobile app is a general news reader which provides curated news feeds and article access; it is age-appropriate and SFW.
The proposal offers a time-boxed ad-free reading experience for viewing a rewarded ad, not for clicking, installing, or rating.
The proposal uses gain framing ('Go Ad-Free for 15 Minutes') and provides a clear 'No thanks' option.
The user initiates the flow from a specific menu item 'Ad-Free Sprint' and must explicitly tap 'Start Sprint' to begin.
The proposal states: 'Play a 15-second game to clear all ads from your news feed for a short sprint.'
The offer includes a 'No thanks' button which dismisses the invitation without penalty.
The offer is accessed from the Account Menu Sidebar, a static navigation surface, and never interrupts an article view or generation.
The proposal explicitly gates the offer to 'Non-paying users currently exposed to standard ad density.'

scores.evidence: The sidebar menu is an occasional-use surface (m10), not a moment of high friction where ad-free reading is the primary user need.
The design is simple and non-intrusive, and it provides a clear value exchange for the reader without degrading existing content.
The 15-minute time box is a 'taste of premium' that functions as a sampler without replacing the value of a potential ad-free tier.
Code-computed earnings per view ($0.009–0.015) well cover the cost of a 15-minute ad-suppression session (COGS 0).
Sidebar navigation (s11) is an occasional reach surface (m2, m10), unlike the core news feed loops (m1, m3, m4).
Uses standard SIM-RWD; the UI integration is straightforward (a menu item in the sidebar).
Uses generic AOL branding for the Game Partner; could be more specific to AOL news categories (e.g., 'AOL Headline Guide').
Capped at 3/day with a 60-minute cooldown, preventing repetitive nagging.
Primary metric (sessions started), guardrails (CTR, retention), and a 21-day user-level holdout are defined.

requiredChanges: Move the entry point from the Account Menu Sidebar (s11) to a more frequent-reach surface, such as a banner or toggle in the Home News Feed (s01/s02) or Article Details (s03), to increase opt-in rates.
Refine the Game Partner persona from 'AOL' to a more thematic entity (e.g., 'AOL News Editor') to improve immersion.
Clarify whether the 'Ad-Free' experience includes the 'Taboola advertising section' mentioned in the digest (e47, e48), as this is a high-density ad element.
parsed.topConcern: The entry point in the Account Menu Sidebar is too deep in the app's hierarchy; the ad-free benefit should be surfaced where the user experiences the ad density (the news feed) to maximize utility and engagement.
